subject.title: [Feature] Prime-number default scheduling for HEARTBEAT / cron “every” + deterministic per-agent phase jitter (anti top-of-hour spikes)

question: Should OpenClaw add public phase, stagger, or prime-cadence controls for cron `every` schedules and heartbeat defaults, or keep `every` as a fixed anchored interval while limiting anti-herd behavior to heartbeat phase spreading and cron expressions?
rationale: The remaining request changes public scheduling semantics and persisted config/API shape, and repository policy treats config/default additions as compatibility-sensitive product direction.

options.title: Design narrow phase/stagger contract
options.body: Add one explicit cron `every` and heartbeat anti-herd contract with schema, CLI, docs, persistence, and upgrade tests before implementation.

options.title: Keep `every` fixed
options.body: Preserve current fixed-interval semantics and close or mark the cron `every` portion not planned while relying on existing heartbeat phase and cron-expression stagger.

options.title: Accept broader prime mode
options.body: Adopt prime cadence transforms plus deterministic phase controls as a larger product surface with migration, observability, and compatibility proof.

recommendation.title: Design narrow phase/stagger contract
recommendation.body: Add one explicit cron `every` and heartbeat anti-herd contract with schema, CLI, docs, persistence, and upgrade tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the existing cron stagger surface and are the strongest routing candidate for the cron scheduling product boundary.
